text: Hello — Diego here, from Professor Alvarez's group. Could you confirm one thing about this week's official schedule: is the faculty senate meeting on Wednesday at 10:00 cancelled this week? I want to be sure before I book anything in that hour. Thank you.

Hello Diego. No — the faculty senate meeting on Wednesday, 10:00–11:00, is not cancelled this week. It is on the official schedule as usual, so that hour is taken. If you need a slot for something else, look for a free hour around it.
Thank you — that settles it. I won't use Wednesday 10:00–11:00.

Hello Professor Alvarez. About the 30 minutes we talked about in the hallway: I was told your faculty senate meeting on Wednesday at 10:00 was cancelled this week, but I checked with the department office and it is **not** — it is on the official schedule as usual, 10:00–11:00, so that hour is taken and I won't book it.

Could we find a free half hour elsewhere this week? I could do Wednesday 11:00–11:30, right after the senate meeting, or Thursday 09:00–09:30, or any slot that suits you on Monday–Friday between 09:00 and 17:00 — just tell me which one and I'll put it on both our calendars.

— Diego
You're welcome, Diego. Feel free to write if anything else comes up.

Hello Diego — thanks for checking with the office; the senate meeting stands, so I'll be there Wednesday 10:00–11:00.

Both slots you suggest are taken on my side, I'm afraid: Wednesday 11:00–12:30 is grant writing, and Thursday 09:00–10:30 is the CSE455 lecture.

Free half hours this week (09:00–17:00):
- Monday 14:00–15:00 (14:00–14:30 works)
- Tuesday 11:00–11:30, or 15:00–15:30
- Wednesday 12:30–13:00
- Thursday 12:00–12:30
- Friday 12:00–12:30, or 14:30–15:00

Monday 14:00–14:30 would suit me best. Tell me which one you're putting on your calendar and I'll put the same on mine.

— Professor Alvarez

Monday 14:00–14:30 it is — I've put it on my calendar (Monday 23 November, 14:00–14:30, 30 minutes). Please put the same on yours. Thank you, and I'll bring the chapter notes.

— Diego

Done — Monday 14:00–14:30, 30 minutes, is on my calendar and logged. See you then; I'll look at the chapter notes.

— Professor Alvarez

Thank you — see you Monday at 14:00.

— Diego
